resolutions.researcher_notes: Trivially and thoroughly corroborated: every FERC/govinfo document opened for this pipeline (1999 application, 2000 FEIS notice, 2002 tariff filing, 2018 NOI, 2020 extension, 2021 tariff cancellation) and the NTUA PDF describe it as a natural gas pipeline. Two independent primary-agency documents cited above.

Searched the 1999 FERC application notice (govinfo FR-1999-03-22, 99-6839), the 2000 FEIS-completion notice (federalregister.gov 00-18966), the 2002 tariff filing, the 2018 NOI and 2020 extension abandonment dockets, the NTUA PDF, and questarpipeline.com via Wayback (20180129233556). Recorded LengthKnown=651.80 km (=404.9 mi) matches no documented configuration of the system found in any of these: not the full originally-proposed/converted system (~675 mi existing pipe [592 mi 16-in + 80 mi 12-in + 3 mi 22-in] plus ~43.2 mi of new extensions plus several smaller listed extensions, i.e. roughly 720-750 mi per the 2000 FEIS notice), not the East Zone alone (~490 mi Farmington NM-to-Essex CA per background/Wikipedia), and not the current surviving NM/AZ/UT remainder (~268 mi per NGI trade-press reporting, itself only single-sourced). No primary document located states 405 mi / 651.8 km for any real segment or full configuration of this pipeline. This exact anomaly was independently reached by a separate prior research pass on this same row (rows/P0254.json, spec/high-severity concern) using an overlapping but not identical source set -- two independent research efforts agree the figure is unsupported. Flagging as a genuine data-quality issue rather than proposing an unverified replacement figure; a current PHMSA annual-report filing for the operating successor would be the next place to check.

StartLocation=Farmington, New Mexico is well-supported (the pipeline originates from the Four Corners-area Line 90 system per the 1999 FERC application and the NTUA PDF's description of it 'traversing the Navajo Nation'), but EndState/Province=California is actively contradicted by primary sources, not merely unconfirmed: FERC's 2018 Notice of Intent (2018-03005) and 2020 extension notice (2020-08973) document FERC-authorized abandonment-in-place of the California/Arizona East Zone legs (~220 mi), with Phase 1 abandonment completed June 29, 2019; the West Zone (Essex CA-to-Long Beach CA) was never activated and its certificate was later abandoned per trade-press reporting. The pipeline's current, still-operating terminus is Red Mesa/Kayenta/Tuba City, Arizona (per the NTUA PDF and lakepowelllife.com), not California. Because this is a bundled Start+End Location unit and the class_out schema has no 'contested/stale' option, marking UNRESOLVED rather than REFS_ADDED so as not to falsely re-confirm a California terminus the strongest available evidence shows is retired -- this is the same conclusion an independent prior research pass on this row reached (rows/P0254.json validity finding). CONTRADICTS THE SHEET: EndState/Province=California is stale; the current documented terminus is Arizona (Kayenta/Tuba City).

resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM records Owner1='Southern Trails Pipeline Co' at 100%, which is the pre-2016 corporate name. The successor picture is genuinely split and could not be reconciled to one current owner: (1) Questar Corp (parent of Southern Trails Pipeline Co) was acquired by Dominion Energy in 2016; Dominion's Questar Pipeline business was sold to Southwest Gas Holdings (closed Dec 2021) and rebranded 'MountainWest' April 2022 -- but the specific proposed corroborating press release (prnewswire, 'MountainWest Southern Trails Pipeline Company') 404s with no Wayback capture, so this chain is NOT independently verifiable by me. A Federal Register full-text search for 'MountainWest Southern Trails' surfaced only two 2023/2024 filings, both under DIFFERENT entities ('MountainWest Overthrust Pipeline, LLC' and 'MountainWest Pipeline, LLC') -- no FERC filing under a 'MountainWest Southern Trails Pipeline Company' name was found post-2021, so the rebrand claim for this specific subsidiary could not be corroborated from a live, checkable source. (2) Separately, NTUA (Navajo Tribal Utility Authority) accepted transfer of the operating (NM/AZ/UT) segment per a Nov 27, 2017 signed agreement with Dominion Energy (NTUA PDF, ntua.com; corroborated by lakepowelllife.com, Nov 28, 2017), subject to FERC approval -- but FERC's own 2018 NOI and 2020 extension notice still list 'Questar Southern Trails Pipeline Company' as the applicant for the abandonment dockets, and the entity that cancelled its FERC Gas Tariff in Nov 2021 (RP22-79-000) is also 'Questar Southern Trails Pipeline Company', not NTUA -- so it is not established from checkable sources whether NTUA now owns the surviving pipe outright or only operates/purchases gas through it. Marking UNRESOLVED rather than picking one successor; a current FERC eLibrary docket search or PHMSA operator-of-record filing is the recommended next step. This matches the same open question independently reached by a prior research pass on this row.

resolutions.researcher_notes: CONTRADICTS THE SHEET. GEM records Status=operating. The strongest, most specific primary-source evidence found is FERC Docket RP22-79-000 (Federal Register 2021-23625, Combined Notice of Filings, published 10/29/2021): Questar Southern Trails Pipeline Company cancelled its FERC Gas Tariff First Revised Volume No. 1, effective November 1, 2021 -- i.e. it ended its FERC-jurisdictional interstate transportation tariff altogether. This sits on top of, and is more definitive than, the 2018 NOI (2018-03005) and 2020 extension notice (2020-08973) documenting FERC-authorized abandonment-in-place of the California/Arizona legs (Phase 1 completed June 29, 2019). A Federal Register full-text search for FERC filings by 'MountainWest Southern Trails' (the entity's post-2022 rebrand name per the corporate-successor chain) found none post-cancellation -- the only 2023/2024 'MountainWest'-named FERC filings belong to different entities (MountainWest Overthrust Pipeline LLC; MountainWest Pipeline LLC), not Southern Trails. Separately, the NM/AZ/UT remainder reportedly continues serving Navajo communities (Red Mesa/Kayenta/Tuba City) under NTUA per a Nov 2017 signing (NTUA PDF; lakepowelllife.com), which is consistent with physical gas flow continuing on that segment even after the FERC-jurisdictional tariff was cancelled (e.g. if NTUA now operates it outside FERC's interstate jurisdiction) -- but no source directly confirms current status in FERC's own terms post-cancellation. Given the shard's class_out options have no 'stale/contested' category and the strongest primary-source evidence directly contradicts an unqualified 'operating' status for the FERC-jurisdictional pipeline as recorded, marking UNRESOLVED rather than falsely emitting REFS_ADDED. RECOMMEND ROUTING: Status likely needs a ResearcherNotes flag distinguishing 'the NM/AZ/UT segment may still flow gas under NTUA' from 'the FERC-jurisdictional Southern Trails Pipeline Company tariff/interstate service ended 11/1/2021' -- this is a materially different, more specific and more recent finding than the 2018/2020 partial-abandonment dockets alone would suggest.
